mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Ultimate Shareholder/Parent Entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry or Registrar of Companies in the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the designated Apostille authority; for non-member countries, Consular Legalization by the Korean Embassy/Consulate with jurisdiction. The two paths are separate and mutually exclusive; an Apostille is never followed by consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificate of Existence)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or tax authority of the parent/UBO's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille certification under the Hague Apostille Convention; non-member states use Consular Legalization at the Korean diplomatic mission only. Do not add an Apostille after consular action.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of the Parent Company authorizing KR_YUHANGHOESA incorporation and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the parent company, certified by the corporate secretary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization by a local public notary, then Apostille by the competent authority; if the origin state is not an Apostille Contracting State, use Consular Legalization by the Korean Consulate. The Apostille and consular routes are alternatives and cannot be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association (Charter) and Amendments of the UBO/Parent Entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Parent company's statutory registry or official government gazette
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille certificate from the Apostille member state's designated authority; otherwise, Consular Legalization by the Korean Consulate. Never use both sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the UBO/Parent funding source
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relationship bank of the UBO or parent, signed by an authorized bank officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank letter with notarized signature; thereafter Apostille if the parent country is an Apostille party. For non-Apostille jurisdictions, use Korean Consular Legalization, not an Apostille.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Every director, shareholder, ultimate beneficial owner, signatory, and commercial counterpart must be screened against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN list, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the Korean FIU-designated persons and prohibited transaction list. PEPs, or persons known to be politically exposed, require senior-management approval of the relationship under Article 5-2 of the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information. Screening must be repeated within five working days before every disbursement and upon any negative media alert; findings must be logged with a timestamp and retained for five years. A positive hit triggers an immediate suspicious transaction report to the Korean FIU, pending transaction freeze, and compliance escalation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Supreme Court of Korea Electronic Registration and Company Name Clearance Portal (Internet Registry Office)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under Article 19 of the Commercial Act, the trade name of a Yuhan Hoesa must be written in Hangul and must include a legal form designation such as Yuhan Hoesa. A foreign-language name may be registered only as a supplementary transliterated name. The four-tier naming convention comprises (1) distinctive mark, (2) business objective and industry, (3) legal liability suffix, and (4) unique registry number. Phonetic transliteration to Hangul is mandatory for any English or Chinese brand name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may request a review of the registry's comparison report within 30 days, submitting the name search certificate and legal grounds showing that the proposed name is distinguishable. If rejected, an administrative appeal may be filed with the Central Administrative Appeals Commission under the Administrative Adjudication Act within 90 days of the notice. A final administrative lawsuit may be filed with the Korean Administrative Court within 90 days after the adjudication result. Counsel should rely on Article 23 of the Commercial Act and relevant precedents requiring the distinctive portion of the name to be visually and phonetically distinct.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Korean registry and tax authorities generally accept a registered agent address only for non-operational entities, but for an anti-dumping trade defense consultancy, the National Tax Service and Korean banks require a physically operating office where books and records are kept, because VAT registration and corporate bank account opening trigger on-site verification. A commercial mailbox is rejected by local tax authorities and financial institutions under the Real Name Financial Transactions Act if no subordinate employee or independent office exists. Therefore, a minimal physical office with a corporate secretary is recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) lease contract in the company's name, (2) business registration card on premises, (3) signage and reception facilities, (4) original books and records, (5) payroll and social insurance records, (6) access to online banking terminal. Quantified risk: approximately 12% annual likelihood for new companies in the ISIC 7490 legal consulting category, rising to 25% if the registered address is classified as a shared office or relay office. Municipal tax inspectors and registry officers can appear unannounced under Article 81 of the Framework Act on National Taxes.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as subsequently amended), Articles 5, 54, 179, 287-2 through 287-45 (Yuhan Hoesa / limited liability company), 289, 317 and 318; Enforcement Decree of the Commercial Act; Business Registration and Tax Acts
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Court Registration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea, territorial branch of the District Court having jurisdiction over the registered office, e.g., Seoul Central District Court Civil Registry Division
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Chunghwa) and Registration of Incorporation Application (Creation Registration)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None under the Korean Commercial Act for a Yuhan Hoesa; no statutory minimum capital is required. However, if capital is declared in the Articles of Incorporation, it must be fully paid into a domestic Korean bank account in the Company's name before registration and shall be held in an escrow-like blocked deposit evidenced by a bank receipt. The capital may be used for business immediately after the registry certificate is issued, but the initial deposit proof must accompany the incorporation filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION IN WRITING BY UNANIMOUS CONSENT OF YUHAN HOESA (LIMITED LIABILITY COMPANY), A REPUBLIC OF KOREA COMPANY IS HEREBY ADOPTED ON THIS [DATE]. WHEREAS the founders of Yuhan Hoesa, a limited liability company (Yuhan Hoesa) organized under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, have duly executed and notarized the Articles of Incorporation; WHEREAS the application for the registration of incorporation has been filed with the competent Court Registration Office and the certificate of incorporation has been or will be issued; WHEREAS the Company is organized to conduct international anti-dumping trade defense consulting, export-import legal advisory services, trade remedy analysis, and related professional activities; AND WHEREAS the Board of Directors is authorized to take all lawful actions necessary to complete the corporate organization and to commence the Company's business operations; NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED, ADOPTED AND CONFIRMED AS FOLLOWS: 1. The subscription of one hundred percent of the issued membership units or shares as stated in the Articles of Incorporation is hereby ratified and confirmed in all respects. The representative director is directed to deposit the fully subscribed paid-in capital into a domestic bank account opened in the Company's name and to preserve the bank deposit confirmation with the corporate records. 2. The registered office of the Company shall be fixed at [seoul or other city, precise address], Republic of Korea, and that address is hereby adopted as the Company's statutory seat, legal domicile for service of process, tax assessment, and official correspondence. Registered office changes shall be approved by the Board and registered with the Court Registry Office. 3. The Board hereby authorizes the opening and maintenance of corporate bank accounts, including domestic accounts and foreign currency accounts where necessary for international wire transfers, with signatory authority vested in any one joint signatory together with the chief financial officer for amounts above KRW Ten Million; for all other matters, any two directors jointly shall sign. 4. The following statutory officers are hereby appointed with immediate effect: (a) [Name] as Chief Executive Officer and Representative Director; (b) [Name] as Chief Financial Officer; and (c) [Name] as Company Secretary. Each officer shall hold office until resignation, removal, or successor appointment, and shall have the power to execute, deliver, and file all corporate documents, banking instructions, tax submissions, and client advisory agreements within the scope of this Resolution. 5. The Chief Executive Officer is directed to apply for the local business registration certificate, VAT registration, and corporate income tax identification number with the National Tax Service; to effect any professional or statutory licensing required for cross-border trade remedy services; and to maintain all corporate books, minutes, and statutory records at the registered office. 6. The Board resolves that all officers, delegates, and attorneys shall be authorized to represent the Company before courts, administrative agencies, customs authorities, and any foreign government bodies in matters concerning the Company's corporate existence and licensing. 7. This Resolution is effective immediately upon adoption and shall continue in force until revoked by a subsequent written resolution. The Chairperson is directed to certify a conformed copy of this Resolution and to deliver it to the Registry, the National Tax Service, banks, insurers, and the Company's professional advisers. THIS RESOLUTION IS FULLY RATIFIED, ADOPTED, AND ORDERED BY THE BOARD ON [DATE].

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Reservation and Articles of Incorporation Preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Internet Registration Office (IRO) of the Supreme Court of Korea, administered through territorial District Court Registry Offices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before the incorporation filing, the founders must complete the name reservation process for the proposed Yuhan Hoesa through the IRO online portal or in person at the competent district court registry. The applicant must select a Korean corporate name that does not conflict with existing company names, submit the required identity documents, and draft the Articles of Incorporation covering objects, principal office, contribution amounts, internal governance, and the initial capital. If the founders are non-residents, a power of attorney must be notarized abroad and legalized by apostille or by the relevant Korean consulate. The Articles must be reviewed for compliance with the Commercial Act, including provisions on the division of profits, officers, accounts, and liquidation. Any defect in the name or contents will cause the registry to suspend the application.
required_dossiers: Passport or certificate of personal identification of all founders and foreign international participants
Notarized power of attorney, if any founder is not physically present
Proposed company name reservation confirmation number
Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean language (with English translation if required by the bank)
Certificate of sole beneficial ownership or indicative ownership statement
Proof of registered office availability or signed lease agreement for the proposed seat
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name reservation is rejected due to similarity with an existing trademark or company name, the founders should immediately file a new name reservation with two or three alternative names and re-submit the Articles with the corrected corporate name. If the registry requests corrections to the Articles, the applicants must cure the indicated items within the statutory peremptory period, normally 14 days, and provide a revised notarized version if notarization has already been completed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of Articles and Filing of Incorporation Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korean notary public in the district of the registered office and the Court Registration Office of the local District Court, either online via IRO or in submission at the registry counter
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Articles of Incorporation have been finalized and the name reservation confirmed, all incorporators or their duly authorized attorneys must appear before a Korean notary to execute and authenticate the Articles. The notary verifies the identity, capacity, and power of the founders and certifies execution. Thereafter, the application for registration of incorporation is submitted to the competent District Court Registry Office. The submission must include the notarized Articles, proof of payment of the incorporation registration tax, a copy of the capital fixed at the time of establishment, and a confirmation of paid-in capital issued by a Korean bank where applicable. The registry then records the Company in the commercial registration register and issues the Certificate of Registration. Any omissions in the filing or payment will delay issuance.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation (two originals)
Incorporation registration application form (prescribed form)
Confirmation of capital deposit from a Korean bank account in the Company's name, if capital is declared
Payment receipt for registration and education tax
Proof identifying all officer appointments and authorized representatives
Legalized apostille or consular certified power of attorney for non-resident incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction notice or suspension order, the applicant must examine the stated deficiencies, file a supplementary response within the statutory quarantine period, and pay any additional registry fee. Where capital contribution proof is missing or insufficient, the registrants must obtain a proper bank certificate and resubmit. If the registry denies the filing entirely, an administrative rectification application may be lodged, and new registration may be filed after curing the grounds for disqualification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and National Tax Service Identity Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS), Business Registration Division of the local District Tax Office having jurisdiction over the statutory registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the Certificate of Incorporation has been issued, the Company must file for business registration under the Framework Act on Taxes and the Value-Added Tax Act at the competent district tax office, either online through the Home Tax Service system or by in-person submission. The application must state the Company's corporate name, registered office address, representative director, and business activities, and must be submitted within 21 days of the incorporation date or the opening of business, whichever is earlier. The tax office will issue a Tax Identification Number, and the Company shall register for corporate income tax, value-added tax, and employer withholding tax. The officers must also establish the actual place of the registered office to allow documentary verification, and for consulting operations, no industrial permit is required.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation issued by the Court Registry
Notarized Articles of Incorporation (certified copy)
Business registration application form (NTS prescribed form)
Identification of the representative director and officer list
Lease agreement for registered office and a copy of building owner documentation
Power of attorney if a tax agent is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office suspends the business registration due to missing address proof, the taxpayer must submit the lease agreement, registered building ownership registry, or a consent letter of the building owner. If the business classification code is challenged, the company must explain its professional consulting scope and may amend the application. Where the NTS initiates a field inspection, the representative director should provide organizational documents and substantive office access. Rejection or non-correction can result in the imposition of a business registration penalty, so immediate supplemental filings are required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening, Swift Wire Access, and Post-Registration Corporate Governance Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banks in the Republic of Korea (e.g., Kookmin, Shinhan, Woori, KEB Hana, or any licensed bank with foreign exchange dealing capacity) and the Court Registry for subsequent director or office-change filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within the first week after business registration, the Company shall open a corporate bank account in the Republic of Korea. The representative director shall present the Certificate of Incorporation, business registration certificate, Articles of Incorporation, and a certified copy of the First Board Resolution approving the bank and signatories. The bank's compliance unit will conduct customer due diligence, including identification of beneficial ownership and source of funds under the Financial Action Task Force standards. For international anti-dumping consultancy fees payable through SWIFT wires or wire transfers, the Company must also complete foreign exchange transaction declarations and submit a corporate foreign exchange identification number application. After account opening, the Board shall adopt or execute any outstanding governance documents, including director appointment certificates, office lease records, and statutory registers, and any changes must be filed in the commercial register.
required_dossiers: Company registration certificate and business registration certificate
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
First Board Resolution authorizing account opening and signatories
Passports and identification cards of authorized signatories
Beneficial ownership chart and source of funds declaration
Corporate foreign exchange identification form, if applicable
Lease agreement or proof of corporate office premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the intended activity or requests enhanced due diligence because the business is legal consulting in cross-border trade defense, the Company must submit a practice description, engagement letters, and clear client and source-of-fund evidence. Should the bank require the physical signature of an offshore director, a notarized and apostilled power of attorney must be delivered. If the Registry issues a deficiency notice for a post-incorporation filing, the Company must file a correction statement through its statutory representative and pay appropriate amendment fees. If the Foreign Exchange Bank refuses the SWIFT wire onboarding, the Company may apply to another licensed bank with the complete KYC package.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; official online electronic portal: HomeTax at hometax.go.kr. Customs clearance and export declaration processing are administered by Korea Customs Service (KCS) through the UNI-PASS system at unipass.customs.go.kr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident entity establishing or participating in a Korean Yuhan Hoesa must apply for business registration with the competent local district tax office through HomeTax within 20 days from the commencement of the Korean business. The application is the statutory Business Registration Application under the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Value-Added Tax Act, and must be accompanied by the articles of incorporation, proof of foreign investment registration under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, paid-in capital evidence, registered office lease or title evidence, identification documents of the representative, and a corporate seal certificate. The NTS issues a 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN), which serves simultaneously as the entity TIN and VAT registration number for a general taxable person. There is no separate VAT certificate. A non-resident foreign supplier with no domestic Korean place of business but with a Korean VAT nexus must register under the NTS non-resident VAT registration procedure through a designated tax representative and obtain the same 10-digit registration number for VAT filing, electronic tax invoices and refund claims.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. The Republic of Korea does not provide a check-the-box election or elective pass-through classification for a Yuhan Hoesa; under the Korean Commercial Act and tax statutes, a Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily classified as a domestic corporation taxed at the entity level. Hybrid mismatch and anti-arbitrage adjustment rules under the Framework Act on International Tax Coordination apply only to prevent double non-taxation and do not create an elective classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: KRW 0 (no turnover threshold; VAT registration is mandatory for every business operator supplying taxable goods or services in Korea from or before business commencement. The KRW 80 million annual turnover simplified taxable person threshold is available only to individual entrepreneurs and is not available to a Yuhan Hoesa corporation, which is always a general taxable person).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: A Yuhan Hoesa general taxable person must issue tax invoices for all taxable supplies and transmit electronic tax invoice issue details to the NTS through HomeTax or an NTS-certified API/commercial e-invoicing system. Korea does not operate a physical fiscal stamping or continuous real-time central clearance model; anti-fraud control is instead achieved through mandatory electronic tax invoice transmission, NTS invoice registry verification, the cash receipt system for consumer supplies, and real-time data matching against Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS export declarations and foreign exchange bank settlement records. Zero-rated export invoices must be distinctly recorded as export/foreign-earning supplies and linked to the underlying export evidence.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export zero-rating is available under the Value-Added Tax Act Article 21 for goods that are physically exported from Korea and for services, including professional anti-dumping and trade-remedy defense consulting, supplied to a non-resident recipient and actually used or consumed outside Korea. The claim requires the supplier to demonstrate that the service was performed for a foreign principal, that no domestic Korean taxable use occurred, that consideration is payable in foreign currency, and that the foreign exchange proceeds are actually repatriated and settled through a Korean foreign exchange bank. Input VAT attributable to zero-rated exports is creditable and recoverable through the periodic VAT return and refund procedure on HomeTax.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Export Cargo Declaration) filed through Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS; for exported services without physical customs clearance, the substitute evidence is the executed service agreement, service delivery or completion report, and evidence of the non-resident recipient status and actual use of the service outside Korea
Bill of Lading for sea cargo or Air Waybill for air cargo, plus commercial invoice and packing list, for goods exports
Zero-rated tax invoice issued under the Korean electronic tax invoice system and transmitted to NTS via HomeTax, expressly marked as an export or foreign-currency-earning supply

Foreign Exchange Bank Export Proceeds Settlement Certificate issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank, being the Korean statutory equivalent of an Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC), evidencing timely receipt and settlement of the export consideration in foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service cross-match HomeTax zero-rated VAT returns with UNI-PASS export declarations and foreign exchange bank settlement records. If export or foreign-use substantiation is incomplete, if foreign exchange is not repatriated within the statutory 180-day period, or if the invoice value does not reconcile with the settled export proceeds, the zero-rating is retrospectively denied and the supply is reclassified as taxable domestic supply. The NTS will assess VAT at 10% on the consideration, impose statutory penalty tax additions including up to 40% penalty tax for fraudulent or grossly negligent underreporting, and assess e-invoice issuance and transmission penalties. False zero-rated invoices or export declarations also expose the entity and its representative to criminal sanctions, fines, and imprisonment under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act and related customs legislation. Retrospective assessments follow the national tax limitation rules: generally 5 years from the date of assessment, extended to 10 years for fraudulent evasion cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK), together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) as the central administrative agency under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; authorized Korean foreign exchange banks handle reporting and control.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a highly liberalised current-account regime; the Korean won is fully convertible for trade in goods, services, dividends, interest, royalties, and ordinary business expenses, provided settlement occurs through an authorized foreign exchange bank. Capital-account transactions remain subject to the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and require either direct reporting, ex-ante notification, or licensed prior approval depending on the specific financial instrument. A capital contribution into a Korean LLC by a foreign investor is treated as foreign direct investment and must be reported under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; subsequent profit remittances are permitted once corporate tax and withholding obligations on dividends are satisfied. There are no general surrender requirements obliging a Korean exporter to convert foreign exchange, but export proceeds must be repatriated to a domestic foreign exchange bank within the statutory collection period. During crisis, Korea may reimpose conversion or payment deferral measures, but the current peacetime regime is open current account plus managed capital account.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export proceeds must be received through an authorized foreign exchange bank and repatriated into Korea within 18 months from the date of the export declaration. There is no fixed statutory ratio for mandatory conversion into KRW; the obligation is focused on collection, receipt, and repatriation of the export foreign currency. The exporter may retain export proceeds in a foreign currency deposit or convert at will, provided the transaction is properly declared through the Foreign Exchange Information System. Extensions beyond the 18-month period require prior approval or reporting to the relevant authorized bank with supporting justification such as trade dispute resolution or financing arrangement.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Non-viable as principal banking rail. Offshore digital EMI providers are not licensed as Korean electronic financial service providers under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act and are not authorized foreign exchange banks under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. They cannot maintain domestic settlement accounts, provide escrow-capable KRW current account services, or perform corporate KYC for foreign direct investment. Using such EMIs for entity treasury would bypass regulated FX reporting and constitute a compliance violation; rated Low viability.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatorily required. A statutory director or a designated financial officer holding a notarized power of attorney must appear in-branch at the Korean bank for a face-to-face interview. Non-resident individual principals may complete consular notarization remotely for signature authentication, but the Korean LLC must present original corporate documents with apostille or consular legalization. Pure remote opening or consular-proxy account opening is not permitted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder and beneficial owner identity concealment through nominee holdings or opaque LLC membership interests.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Korean corporate registry; registered memorandum and articles of association; chain-of-title ownership chart; notarized identification and corporate documents for all direct and indirect natural persons with 25% or greater ownership; beneficial ownership declaration under Financial Intelligence Unit guidance; and if nominee holding exists, an attested declaration identifying settlor, protector, and ultimate beneficial interest.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the initial capital injection from a non-resident shareholder.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of bank statements of the remitting entity or individual; tax clearance and profit distribution documentation; sale of shares or asset disposal evidence; and a foreign direct investment declaration confirming the capital contribution under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and Foreign Investment Promotion Act.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the declared low-risk consulting business and high-volume cross-border payments received from overseas clients in anti-dumping and trade defense cases.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed client engagement letters; detailed anti-dumping defense retainer agreements; per-matter invoices and fee schedules; supporting work product and procedural submission calendar; and a risk-tagged client list identifying commercial purpose, jurisdiction, and payment terms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Third-party payments or settlements from non-counterparty entities inconsistent with the named account payee.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written authorization signed by the principal client authorizing the third-party payer; a copy of the underlying judgment, award, or settlement; proof of intermediation arrangement; and a compliance undertaking committing to reject unsupported third-party deposits.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: A non-resident shareholder remits USD, EUR, or KRW via SWIFT MT103 to the company's designated account at an authorized Korean foreign exchange bank. The remittance must be pre-notified as a foreign direct investment under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, and the receiving bank will require the corporate registration certificate, board resolution approving the share subscription, and a foreign exchange transaction report with the relevant direct investment capital contribution purpose code. After receipt, the bank issues a foreign exchange transaction confirmation and the statutory capital verification certificate is prepared by a licensed auditor or customs broker where required. The funds are then transferred to the operating account via a controlled internal journal entry with full AML audit trail.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for ordinary service payments, foreign counsel fees, anti-dumping defense case retainer payments, and consultant invoices; Commercial Letters of Credit and Documentary Collections are available for contingent trade remedy bond payments or civil surety obligations, but such instruments should be arranged through the Korean bank's trade finance desk with underlying court orders or regulatory rulings. All outbound disbursements require the submission of the relevant contract, invoice, and a foreign exchange declaration containing the appropriate payment purpose code under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain-vanilla deliverable KRW/USD or KRW/EUR forward contracts with a documented underlying trade, service, or foreign direct investment exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed only with an authorized Korean bank and only for legitimate KRW risk arising from cross-border receivables or payables
Cross-currency swaps permitted strictly for hedging the interest and principal of real cross-border borrowings, not for speculative position-taking

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements and business performance report adopted at the annual general meeting (AGM) of Yuhan Hoesa, together with execution and retention of the statutory minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate secretariat / shareholders' meeting; no government receiving authority for the AGM itself
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 calendar days after the close of the fiscal year; calendar-year entities must hold the AGM no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to hold the AGM within the statutory window renders the officers subject to administrative fines up to KRW 10 million under the Korean Commercial Act; financial statements not timely adopted cannot be validly filed with the National Tax Service, generating separate non-filing penalties; prolonged inactivity and abandonment for at least 5 consecutive years may trigger judicial strike-off and dissolution under Article 520-2 of the Commercial Act.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return including the local income tax surcharge for the fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) and the competent local government where the registered office is located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Paper filing by March 31 following the fiscal year-end; e-filing extension to April 30 for calendar-year Yuhan Hoesa; non-calendar-year filers must file within 3 months by paper or 4 months by e-filing after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or understating tax attracts negligence tax of 10-20% on the understated or unfaithful amount, additional 20% unfaithful tax penalty, and late-payment interest at 0.022% per day (approximately 8.03% per annum) on unpaid tax; repeated failure to file can lead to business registration cancellation, compulsory collection, seizure of bank accounts and receivables, and ultimately administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Semi-annual Value-Added Tax declaration and payment statement (VAT returns)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year taxpayers: first semi-annual return and payment by July 25; second semi-annual return and payment by January 25 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Omitted or incorrectly reported VAT triggers a 10% general negligence penalty (increased to 20% for intentional omission, 30% for unfaithful conversion, and 40% for failure to register) plus 0.022% per-day late-payment interest; persistent non-filing subjects the company to tax-office business closure after a 7-day warning notice and may trigger judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Statutory external audit report submission by the certified CPA auditor to the Financial Supervisory Service and delivery of audited financial statements to shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) / electronic disclosure submission system and shareholders of Yuhan Hoesa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year audited companies, the audit must be completed within 90 days after fiscal year-end (by March 31); the auditor must submit the audit report to the FSS within 15 days of the applicable due date, in practice by April 15 unless an extension is obtained; the audited financial statements must be presented to the AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to appoint an external auditor or obstruction of the audit gives rise to sanctions under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, including designation of an auditor by the Securities and Futures Commission, administrative fines, refusal of the FSS to accept the audit report, and criminal enforcement; absence of a valid audited report also causes provisional tax assessment with 20% under-declared penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-invested enterprise status report, if the Yuhan Hoesa has non-resident equity ownership exceeding the FDI notification threshold
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy / KOTRA or the designated foreign-exchange bank
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within 90 days after fiscal year-end (calendar-year filers by March 31); any change in foreign investor status or shareholding ratio must be reported within 30 days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or filing false information under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act may result in administrative fines up to KRW 10 million, loss of foreign-exchange preferential treatment, corrective orders from the competent authority, and inability to remit dividends under the foreign-investment reporting regime; prolonged failure may trigger administrative penalties and strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner and corporate status confirmation covering the registers of members, directors, charges, and ultimate beneficial owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company statutory registers maintained at the registered office; no separate central annual return in ordinary non-listed cases
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ongoing annual confirmation exercise by December 31 of each year; any membership transfer, director change, charge creation or release, or beneficial-ownership event must be entered in the statutory registers within 30 calendar days of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A transfer of Yuhan Hoesa membership interests is not opposable to the company until entered in the Register of Members; directors who knowingly keep false registers are liable for damages and subject to criminal fines and imprisonment under the Korean Commercial Act; inaccurate beneficial-owner information provided to financial institutions triggers fines under Korea's AML and Financial Information Act and may result in banking-relationship termination, loss of share transfer recognition, and administrative cancellation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, a Yuhan Hoesa is legally required to undergo an independent certified CPA audit when total assets shown on the balance sheet at the end of the immediately preceding fiscal year equal or exceed KRW 12 billion (approximately USD 9.2 million). Turnover and headcount are not standalone statutory audit triggers for ordinary private limited companies; however, the Financial Services Commission may designate a company for mandatory audit where the company exhibits substantial public interest, including cases of revenue in excess of KRW 100 billion, total assets above KRW 7 billion combined with a debt-to-equity ratio above 500%, or an employee headcount exceeding 500, and any designation makes the independent CPA audit compulsorily applicable. For financial-industry supervised entities, lower balance-sheet thresholds may apply. All audits must be performed by an independent Korean certified public accountant or audit firm, not by an internal auditor.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS (Korean International Financial Reporting Standards) for entities adopting IFRS; K-GAAP (Korean Generally Accepted Accounting Principles) for private non-listed Yuhan Hoesa; Korean SME Accounting Standards for eligible small and medium enterprises; the audit engagement itself is conducted under Korea Standards on Auditing (KSA), substantially converged with International Standards on Auditing (ISA).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not impose a single annual UBO return for an ordinary private Yuhan Hoesa. Instead, the company must maintain and update the Register of Members continuously; any transfer of membership interests, pledge, change of control, or change in ultimate natural-person ownership must be documented and entered in the statutory register within 30 calendar days of the event. A mandatory annual UBO confirmation exercise must be performed at fiscal year-end (December 31) by obtaining a beneficial-ownership representation from each registered member, and the same 30-day reporting window applies to notifications to financial institutions under Korea's AML regime. Failure to register a transfer within the statutory window prevents the transferee from asserting rights against the company and exposes responsible directors to penalties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Register of Shareholders/Equity Interests)
Minute Book of Directors and Shareholders Meetings
Business License and Statutory Permit Register

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - 2,500 per annum for registered office / corporate agent services in South Korea
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 15,000 - 45,000 per annum for a certified independent statutory audit of a moderate-size private Korean Yuhan Hoesa

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national headline CIT rate on taxable income above KRW 300 billion (combined 26.4% including the 10% local income tax surcharge; lower progressive brackets apply at 10%, 20% and 22%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign-invested enterprises in Free Economic Zones may receive 100% corporate tax exemption for 5 years and a 50% reduction for 2 further years; R&D expenses can generate super tax credits of 30%-40%; technology-transfer income for SMEs may be exempt or taxed at a reduced rate; anti-dumping trade-defense consulting fees are ordinary business income and do not automatically qualify unless statutory investment/R&D substance is met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return for Tax Base and Tax Amount (domestic corporation) filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the close of the fiscal year; for a December 31 year-end the return and supporting schedules are due by March 31 of the following year, or the next business day if the statutory date falls on a weekend or public holiday.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year, corporate registration number, entity type, head office address, representative director details, and business classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the supplementary shareholder register and disclose all foreign/non-resident shareholders, directors and ultimate beneficial owners. If the representative director is a non-resident without Korean residence, appoint and record a domestic tax representative for service of process and electronic filing communications.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income, aggregate segment revenue, non-taxable income and adjusted total income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean-incorporated LLC is a domestic resident corporation subject to worldwide taxation; include foreign-source dividends, interest, royalties, capital gains and consulting fees. Non-resident shareholders' tax status does not limit the entity-level income inclusion.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses and taxable income reconciliation through additions and deductions (depreciation, bad debts, entertainment expense, related-party payments, reserves).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses paid to overseas related parties must satisfy the arm's-length standard and be evidenced by actual trade-defense services. Payments made solely to shift profits to non-resident shareholders are disallowed and may be recharacterized as constructive dividends subject to withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computation, application of tax-loss carryforward, non-deductible statutory items, and income from foreign branches/P.E.s.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply NOL carryforward within the 10-year limit (15 years for SMEs); allocate core income-generating activities to the Korean entity. Do not offset losses of a foreign permanent establishment unless permitted by the applicable DTA and domestic loss-allocation rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculated corporate income tax, progressive rates, local income tax surcharge, and add-on taxes including minimum taxes and anti-avoidance adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the standard progressive Korean CIT schedule regardless of non-resident shareholding. Uncollected withholding taxes on non-resident remittances are added here, together with daily late-payment surcharges if remittances were made without proper withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax credits, foreign tax credit, R&D/investment credits, preliminary tax payments, and carryover credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Claim foreign tax credits by completing the OECD-compliant schedule and attaching foreign tax receipts. For treaty-based dividend withholding relief, attach the DTA application, the foreign corporate shareholder's Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial ownership evidence before claiming any credit or reduced rate at source.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or non-filing attracts an additional 20% penalty on the unpaid corporate tax; understatement penalties are 10% for negligent misstatements and 40% for fraudulent misstatements; unpaid tax accrues a daily surcharge of approximately 0.022% per day (about 8.03% per annum). Willful tax evasion is punished under the Punishment of Tax Evasion Act by imprisonment for up to five years and/or a fine of up to KRW 100 million or twice the evaded tax. A withholding agent who fails to withhold non-resident tax may be held personally liable for the uncollected WHT and associated penalties.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% combined on gross dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders (20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge), unless reduced by an applicable Double Tax Treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the payor must submit to the NTS before or at the time of distribution: (i) an Application for Non-Resident Corporation Withholding Tax Exemption/Reduction under the relevant treaty; (ii) a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the foreign tax administration; (iii) a beneficial ownership declaration, including the ultimate shareholders and no back-to-back conduit arrangement; and (iv) documentation proving the required shareholding percentage (commonly 25% or more) and holding period under the treaty dividend article. The payer may then apply the reduced treaty rate at source. If no advance treaty clearance is obtained, the statutory 22% must be withheld and a refund application may be made through the NTS treaty-refund procedure within the statutory time limits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Under Korean domestic law, outbound royalties and interest to non-resident corporations are each subject to 20% national WHT plus 2% local income tax surcharge, a combined 22%. Most Korean DTAs reduce interest to 5%-15% and royalties to 0%-15% (commonly 10%-15%), conditional on TRC, beneficial ownership, and compliance with anti-treaty-shopping rules; royalties paid to a shell company without substance will not receive treaty protection.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory where aggregate annual cross-border related-party transactions equal or exceed KRW 10 billion; Master File is required where aggregate related-party transactions equal or exceed KRW 100 billion or the MNE group satisfies the CbCR threshold (consolidated revenue at the statutory threshold, approximately KRW 1 trillion). Simplified contemporaneous documentation is required for all related-party transactions below these thresholds, and documentation must be produced to the NTS within 30 days of request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not apply Gulf-format ESR, but the substance-over-form principle (Framework Act on National Taxes Article 14) and the statutory GAAR allow recharacterization of transactions lacking real economic substance. For anti-dumping defense consulting, the Korean entity must perform Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA), maintain premises and employees, control contracts and decision-making, and bill clients at arm's length. Offshore shell affiliates without substance will be disregarded, and the Korean CFC regime may currently tax passive income accumulated abroad.
